prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Security advisories for affected dependencies (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "CVE ID" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 110px
  col 2: header "Package" · longest unbreakable word 144px · one-line width 144px
  col 3: header "Affected versions" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 297px
  col 4: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 5: header "Summary" · longest unbreakable word 195px · one-line width 2738px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 793px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 792px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [131, 165, 145, 73, 278] · table 793×1401px · row heights [33, 255, 214, 214, 214, 235, 235] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 0

Design r2A: widths [131, 165, 130, 73, 293] · table 793×1361px · row heights [53, 255, 214, 194, 194, 214, 235] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [131, 165, 140, 73, 283] · table 793×1361px · row heights [33, 255, 214, 194, 194, 235, 235] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [131, 165, 126, 73, 297] · table 793×1321px · row heights [53, 255, 194, 194, 194, 214, 214] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [131, 165, 124, 73, 299] · table 793×1300px · row heights [53, 235, 194, 194, 194, 214, 214] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [131, 165, 138, 73, 285] · table 793×1361px · row heights [33, 255, 214, 194, 194, 235, 235] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [131, 165, 155, 73, 268] · table 793×1441px · row heights [33, 275, 214, 214, 235, 235, 235] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 13 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
